fact: Biometric Update reports that Kenya's Maisha Namba digital ID system is expanding, with more than 1.5 million cards produced in the first five months of 2026, per the Principal Secretary for Immigration and Citizen Services.

The government gazetted a six-month waiver of fees for replacing national identification cards and changing particulars under the Registration of Persons (Amendment) Rules, 2025, and President Ruto urged people without a card to apply.

The National Registration Bureau issues national identity cards in Elgeyo Marakwet County, with Live Capture Units sending applicants' data and photographs to Nairobi, per a National Assembly committee statement of 5 October 2026.

The National Registration Bureau registers residents in Bungoma and elsewhere and produces national identity cards at its headquarters, with 19,361 registrations under the new programme in July to September 2026.
National Registration Bureau secretary Gilbert Kitiyo said over 600,000 people without IDs have been registered since extra vetting in border counties ended, with first-time applications free.
Principal Secretary Belio Kipsang said 600 live-capture biometric devices let new national identity cards be issued in 10 days, one day in Nairobi.
Kenya has a national digital ID system, Maisha Namba, which the government considers the foundation of all digital transactions and which is in about its third year of implementation.
The Principal Secretary says the government is rolling out a third-generation digital ID, the Maisha card, moving from the old generation ID.

The Nation says the government rolled out the Maisha number, a unique personal number assigned to the Maisha Card, a third-generation digital ID card, and that registration was cleared to proceed in 2024 after a court challenge.
